items.q: What are the two layers of an agent harness?
items.a: The **runtime** (where the loop runs, resumable state) and the **context and orchestration** layer (models, prompts, tools, compaction).

items.q: What did recent studies find about harness choice on frontier models?
items.a: It **barely changed benchmark scores**, but it did change **cost per task** a lot.

items.q: What did Cursor remove as models got smarter?
items.a: Guardrails like a **separate apply-edit model** and instructions on exploring code and **checking your work**.

items.q: Why do harness tricks become obsolete?
items.a: The **data flywheel**: harder tasks get used, data reaches the labs, and models **absorb the skill natively**.

items.q: Where does the harness go once a skill is commoditised?
items.a: To the **next frontier** of tasks, adding guardrails back for things **models haven't nailed yet**.

items.q: Which new tasks needed guardrails added back in Grok Bot?
items.a: Slide decks and travel, **keeping the user informed** without overload, **acting versus asking**, and memory.

items.q: Why can't long-running agents live on a laptop?
items.a: Tasks now run **hours to days**, so they need **cloud infrastructure** that doesn't sleep.

items.q: Why isn't a bash-plus-secrets harness enough?
items.a: You need **scoped permissions** and guardrails against **catastrophic actions** or a huge API bill.

items.q: Which levers cut harness cost without hurting quality?
items.a: **Cache hit rate**, token efficiency and **model mix**.
A **composable building block**, like one **subscriptions tool** for Slack, CI and time events.

items.q: How should you manage behavioural shims?
items.a: **Log every shim** centrally and let a bot **remove shims that stop firing**.

items.q: Why hide harness internals from users?
items.a: Hyrum's law: users **depend on whatever you expose**, so hiding it lets you **ship and unship fast**.

items.q: Where will most agent work run within six months?
items.a: Katz predicts about **90% off the laptop**, in the cloud.
